chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran said: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Asbat ibn Muhammad, linking it up through a chain of narrators to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said:

Gossiping is worse than adultery. It was said: O Messenger of God, why is that so? He said: The one who commits adultery repents and God accepts his repentance, but the one who gossips repents and God does not accept his repentance until the person he gossiped about forgives him.

key_terms.الْغِيبَةُ: Backbiting (mentioning a person in their absence)
key_terms.يَحِلُّهُ: He forgives him / He grants pardon

ai.seo_question: Why is backbiting considered worse than adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this distinction to emphasize that while adultery is a sin against God (huquq Allah) where divine forgiveness is immediate upon repentation, backbiting is a sin against the individual (huquq al-adami) requiring the victim's pardon. This underscores the necessity of seeking personal forgiveness from the specific person backbitten before God grants absolution, illustrating the dual nature of sins in Shia jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-90 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran , on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn al-Nue’man, on the authority of Asbat ibn Muhammad who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Prophet (MGB), “

Gossiping is worse than committing adultery.” The Prophet (MGB) was asked, “O Prophet of God! How could that be so?” The Prophet (MGB) replied, “One who has committed adultery can repent and God would accept his repentance, but if one who has gossiped repents, God would not accept his repentance until the one he gossiped about forgives him.”
